proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(Z=(y,M,B,s_1)\), with the matrix blocks vectorized in a fixed order, and let
\(\widehat Z=(\widehat y,\widehat M,\widehat B,\widehat s_1)\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel}
makes the dimension of this vector fixed.  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion}, whose hypotheses include
conditional independent censoring, censoring positivity, the stated nuisance rates, and the relative-survival
bounded-variation conditions, gives
\[
 \widehat Z-Z=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_i+r_K,
 \qquad \sqrt K\,\lVert r_K\rVert_2\longrightarrow_P0.
\]
Each component of \(\Phi_i\) is centered by the definition of \(\phi_c\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:cell-iid}
and Assumption~\ref{ass:cross-cell-independence} imply that the vectors \(\Phi_1,\ldots,\Phi_K\) are
independent and identically distributed: their common law is the product, over the fixed cells, of the
corresponding cell laws.  Assumption~\ref{ass:influence-moment}, finiteness of \(\mathcal C\), and
Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} imply
\[
 E\Phi_i=0,
 \qquad E\lVert\Phi_i\rVert_2^{2+\nu}<\infty.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 E\left\lVert K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_i\right\rVert_2^2
 =E\lVert\Phi_i\rVert_2^2<\infty.
\]
Markov's inequality and the first display therefore yield
\[
 \lVert\widehat Z-Z\rVert_2=O_P(K^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \lVert\widehat M-M\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]

Assumption~\ref{ass:exact-rank} gives \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\), while
Assumption~\ref{ass:singular-gap} gives \(\sigma_r(M)\ge\kappa>0\).  Hence \(M_r=M\),
\(P=M^+\), and \(\lVert P\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=\sigma_r(M)^{-1}\le\kappa^{-1}\).
Lemma~\ref{lem:full-spectral-differential} supplies a neighborhood of \((y,M,B)\) on which
\(\mathcal F(y,M,B)=yM_r^+B\) is Fr\'echet differentiable.  Since \(\widehat Z\to_PZ\), the
probability that the estimated blocks lie in that neighborhood tends to one.  The definition of Fr\'echet
differentiability, the preceding root-\(K\) bound, Definition~\ref{def:full-spectral-map}, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:full-spectral-differential} give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\theta-\theta
 &=(\widehat y-y)PB
   +y\mathcal L_M(\widehat M-M)B
   +yP(\widehat B-B)+o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
   \left\{\Phi_{y,i}PB+y\mathcal L_M(\Phi_{M,i})B+yP\Phi_{B,i}\right\}
   +o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\theta,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The factual-post block of Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} is
\[
 \widehat s_1-s_1=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{1,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Stacking these two expansions and applying Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence} proves
\[
 \sqrt K
 \begin{pmatrix}\widehat\theta-\theta\\ \widehat s_1-s_1\end{pmatrix}
 =K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}+o_P(1).
\]
In particular, all three learned spectral blocks contribute: the target-pre term is \(\Phi_{y,i}PB\),
the donor-pre term is \(y\mathcal L_M(\Phi_{M,i})B\), and the donor-post term is
\(yP\Phi_{B,i}\).

Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence} expresses \(\Phi_{\eta,i}\) as a fixed linear transformation
of \(\Phi_i\).  The coefficients of that transformation are finite because the dimensions are fixed,
\(\lVert P\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le\kappa^{-1}\), and the explicit formula in
Definition~\ref{def:full-differential} makes \(\mathcal L_M\) a bounded linear map.  Thus
\[
 E\Phi_{\eta,i}=0,
 \qquad E\lVert\Phi_{\eta,i}\rVert_2^{2+\nu}<\infty,
 \qquad E\{\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^{\top}\}=\Omega_\eta.
\]
For completeness, fix \(a\in\mathbb R^{2J}\), put \(W_i=a^\top\Phi_{\eta,i}\), and set
\(\delta=\min(\nu,1)>0\).  For a finite constant \(C_\delta\), the elementary Taylor bound
\[
 \left|e^{\mathrm i x}-1-\mathrm i x+\frac{x^2}{2}\right|
 \le C_\delta |x|^{2+\delta},\qquad x\in\mathbb R,
\]
follows from the third-order remainder on \(|x|\le1\) and boundedness of \(e^{\mathrm i x}\) on
\(|x|>1\).  With \(\omega_a^2=a^\top\Omega_\eta a\), centering and the preceding moment bound imply
\[
 \left|E e^{\mathrm iW_i/\sqrt K}-1+\frac{\omega_a^2}{2K}\right|
 \le C_\delta K^{-1-\delta/2}E|W_i|^{2+\delta}=o(K^{-1}).
\]
Independence then gives
\[
 E\exp\!\left\{\mathrm i a^\top K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}\right\}
 \longrightarrow\exp(-\omega_a^2/2).
\]
The right-hand side is the characteristic function of \(\mathcal N_{2J}(0,\Omega_\eta)\), so the
continuity criterion for characteristic functions yields
\[
 K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N_{2J}(0,\Omega_\eta).
\]
Together with the asymptotic linear representation, this proves the asserted joint limit.  Moreover,
Assumption~\ref{ass:nondegenerate-covariance} gives
\(a^\top\Omega_\eta a\ge v\lVert a\rVert_2^2\) for every \(a\), so the Gaussian limit is
nondegenerate.

It remains to establish the two plug-in conclusions.  Let \(\Pi_R(A)\) be the orthogonal projector onto
the leading \(r\) right singular vectors of a matrix \(A\) near \(M\).  The variational characterization
of singular values and
\[
 \bigl|\lVert Ax\rVert_2-\lVert Mx\rVert_2\bigr|
 \le\lVert A-M\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\lVert x\rVert_2
\]
imply \(|\sigma_j(A)-\sigma_j(M)|\le\lVert A-M\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\) for each \(j\).  Exact rank and
\(\sigma_r(M)\ge\kappa\) therefore make the leading \(r\)-dimensional subspace unique on a sufficiently
small neighborhood of \(M\).  To verify its continuity, observe that the set of rank-\(r\) orthogonal
projectors is compact and \(\Pi_R(A)\) maximizes
\[
 Q\longmapsto\operatorname{tr}(QA^\top A)
\]
over that set.  If \(A_m\to M\), every convergent subsequence of \(\Pi_R(A_m)\) must maximize
\(Q\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(QM^\top M)\); the singular gap makes that maximizer uniquely
\(\Pi_R(M)\).  Hence \(\Pi_R(A)\to\Pi_R(M)\) and \(A_r=A\Pi_R(A)\to M\).  In a singular-vector basis,
\[
 A_r^+=\left\{A_r^\top A_r+I-\Pi_R(A)\right\}^{-1}A_r^\top.
\]
The matrix in braces has eigenvalues \(\sigma_1(A)^2,\ldots,\sigma_r(A)^2,1,\ldots,1\), which are
bounded away from zero locally.  Continuity of multiplication and inversion therefore gives
\[
 (\widehat M)_r^+\longrightarrow_P P,
 \qquad
 \widehat{\mathcal L}_{\widehat M}\longrightarrow_P\mathcal L_M
\]
in the relevant operator norms, where the second convergence follows by substitution into
Definition~\ref{def:full-differential}.

Let \(\widehat\Phi_i\) be the stack of fold-specific fitted cell influence vectors.  The final assertion of
Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} gives foldwise \(L_2(P_c)\)-consistency.  Conditional on the training
sample for a fold, its validation observations have law \(P_c\), so the conditional expectation of the
validation mean squared error is the corresponding \(L_2(P_c)\) error.  Conditional Markov inequalities
and a union bound over the fixed numbers of cells and folds yield
\[
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\lVert\widehat\Phi_i-\Phi_i\rVert_2^2=o_P(1).
\]
Let \(\mathsf A\) denote the fixed linear operator in Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence}, including
the unchanged factual-post block, and let \(\widehat{\mathsf A}\) be its plug-in version.  Consistency of all
four estimated blocks and the two spectral convergences above imply
\[
 \lVert\widehat{\mathsf A}-\mathsf A\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),
 \qquad \lVert\widehat{\mathsf A}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(1).
\]
Also, Markov's inequality and \(E\lVert\Phi_i\rVert_2^2<\infty\) give
\(K^{-1}\sum_i\lVert\Phi_i\rVert_2^2=O_P(1)\).  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\lVert\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\rVert_2^2
 &\le 2\lVert\widehat{\mathsf A}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\lVert\widehat\Phi_i-\Phi_i\rVert_2^2\\
 &\quad+2\lVert\widehat{\mathsf A}-\mathsf A\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\lVert\Phi_i\rVert_2^2=o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]

Put \(D_i=\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\).  Expanding the difference of outer products and applying
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\left\lVert\widehat\Omega_\eta-K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
 \Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top\right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &\quad\le
 \left\{K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\lVert D_i\rVert_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \left[
 \left\{K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\lVert\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}\rVert_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 +\left\{K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\lVert\Phi_{\eta,i}\rVert_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \right]=o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
For every pair of coordinates \(k,m\), Cauchy--Schwarz makes
\(\Phi_{\eta,i,k}\Phi_{\eta,i,m}\) integrable.  Truncation, Chebyshev's inequality for the bounded
truncations, and removal of the truncation prove the scalar weak law for each entry.  Since \(2J\) is fixed,
\[
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top
 \longrightarrow_P E\{\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top\}=\Omega_\eta.
\]
The preceding two displays prove \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\to_P\Omega_\eta\).

Finally, the observed-law functional and the causal target are distinct.  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion},
under Assumptions~\ref{ass:conditional-censoring} and~\ref{ass:censor-positivity}, centers every cell estimator
at the covariate-standardized event survival \(S_c(t)=E\{Q_c(t\mid X_{ci})\}\).  Thus \(y,M,B,s_1\) are
identified observed-law survival blocks, not marginal Kaplan--Meier pseudo-targets.  Assumption~\ref{ass:target-pre-span}
gives \(y\in\operatorname{row}(M)\).  Separately, Assumption~\ref{ass:post-transport} asserts that the target
unit's untreated post-treatment survival row equals the observed-law functional \(yM_r^+B\).  It is this
identification assumption, rather than the definition of \(\theta\), that equates the functional with the
causal untreated curve.  The row \(s_1\) remains the factual treated survival curve.  Hence the Gaussian law
is centered at the claimed causal and factual targets, completing the proof.

proposed.comparator_claim: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) impose event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, use a fixed-grid latent-factor/PCR transport, and form the spectral inputs from marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves; they do not derive covariate-adjusted AIPCW spectral influence inference.
Published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4) gives asymptotic linearity for a directly estimated cross-fitted doubly robust treatment-specific survival curve.
Theorem 2 and Corollary 2 give row-space out-of-sample prediction guarantees for minimum-norm principal component regression.
Equation (4.12) gives the Fr\'echet derivative of the Moore--Penrose inverse under locally constant rank.
Sections 3--4 show interpolation, variance, and survival-curve bias for synthetic survival individuals.
Theorem 3.1 gives feasible inference for low-rank linear functionals when the working rank overestimates the true rank.

Theorem 2.1 recovers the factor space for bounded working rank at least the true rank as the cross-sectional dimension grows, and Theorem 3.2 with Corollary 3.1 gives over-estimated-rank-robust factor-augmented inference.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The Westling comparator retained the stale published theorem number; the version-explicit verified locator is published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4).

project_justification.gap: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) already state event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, but their spectral workflow uses marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves and does not give a covariate-adjusted joint influence law. With heterogeneous covariates, conditional independence need not imply marginal independence, so those cell inputs can converge to distorted curves before PCR transport. Westling et al. (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4)) provide asymptotic-linearity theory for a directly estimated treatment-specific curve, not for a learned three-block spectral counterfactual.

prose_updates.related_work: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) supply the fixed-grid latent-factor survival panel, unit and time spans, PCR transport, and the 925-patient, 10-country TCL application. They already assume event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates; the present advance is therefore not a weaker censoring premise, but replacement of marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier inputs by covariate-adjusted AIPCW inputs when within-cell covariate heterogeneity creates marginal dependent censoring, together with full transported inference. Proposition~\ref{prop:han-shah-fixed-grid-embedding} gives the exact matrix bridge from their spans to \(y\in\operatorname{row}(M)\) and \(yM_r^+B\), while Proposition~\ref{prop:km-pcr-cancellation} certifies an open class of fixed Kaplan--Meier/PCR bias. Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4) and Sections 5.2--5.3) supply the cross-fitted augmented survival-score architecture and direct-curve asymptotic linearity, but not a data-dependent spectral transport; the substantive relative-survival variation condition imposed here is stronger than their ordinary product-rate bookkeeping. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025, Theorem 2 and Corollary 2) clarify minimum-norm PCR and row-space prediction without censoring-aware asymptotics. Golub and Pereyra (1973, equation (4.12)) are the matrix-calculus ancestor for the constant-rank pseudoinverse derivative. Curth, Poon, Nori, and Gonz\'alez (2024, Sections 3--4) analyze survival synthetic-control bias but do not derive this three-block PCR pseudo-limit or its relatively open nonzero-bias region. Fan and Liao (2022) and Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2026) address growing-panel or rank-robust factor inference rather than the fixed-dimension separated-rank theorem proved here.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved results cover only the fixed-panel, fixed-grid, exact-rank, fixed-singular-gap, exact-span, and exact-post-transport subclass. They additionally require within-cell i.i.d. sampling, independence of the samples across cells, conditional independent censoring, a common positive censor-survival bound, nondegenerate transported covariance, fixed-fold nuisance consistency and product rate, event-origin normalization, and the substantive bounded-variation and \(L_2\) variation-rate restrictions on fitted relative-survival paths. The joint-cell lemma is proved under those restrictions; the spectral limit, fixed-grid band, and grid-RMST interval inherit them transitively. The Han--Shah embedding is algebraic and supplies none of the within-cell sampling, cross-cell independence, censoring, covariance, or learner conditions. In particular, applying the theorem's standard errors or targeting interpretation to the 925-patient repeated-treatment-line TCL analysis requires those sampling and learner conditions to be verified for that application; the algebraic embedding alone does not verify cross-cell independence. The rational \(2\times2\) witness belongs to the fixed-grid factor/span subclass, while its negative Kaplan--Meier/PCR conclusion does not require the positive theorem's learner assumptions. Nothing here covers growing donor or time dimensions, a growing post grid, a shrinking or closed singular gap, selected rank, covariance degeneracy, approximate transport, or continuous-time RMST. The weak-gap and rank-selection problem remains the clear tier-changing follow-up, so the present contribution is a solid specialized fixed-grid result rather than a flagship general theory.

statement_notes.gap: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) assume conditional independent censoring given treatment and covariates but analyze marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier/PCR inputs; Westling et al. (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4)) analyze a directly estimated covariate-adjusted survival curve without learned spectral transport. Neither gives this full three-block influence vector or its joint covariance law.
statement_notes.consumer: If the within-cell i.i.d., cross-cell independence, and stated nuisance-learner conditions are verified for the 925-patient, 10-country TCL analysis, the theorem could provide standard errors for the untreated United States curve and its contrast with observed single-agent therapy; the application itself is not taken to verify those conditions.

The bridge supplies the fixed-grid targeting map for the untreated United States post-treatment curve when the stated Han--Shah spans hold. In the 925-patient, 10-country TCL application, inference based on that map could be used only if this note's within-cell i.i.d., cross-cell independence, censoring, covariance, and learner conditions are separately verified; the algebraic bridge does not establish them.
